notes:
1. Subhas Chandra Bose — Overview

  • Subhas Chandra Bose was one of the most dynamic nationalist leaders of the Indian freedom struggle.
  • He advocated complete independence from British rule.
  • He differed from Mahatma Gandhi over strategy and the pace of the national movement.
  • During the Second World War, he sought international military assistance to overthrow British rule.
  • He became the supreme leader of the Indian National Army and the Provisional Government of Azad Hind.
📌 Must-Memorise

Subhas Chandra Bose → Forward Bloc + INA + Azad Hind Government

2. Popular Title

  • Subhas Chandra Bose is popularly known as Netaji.
📌 Must-Memorise

Netaji → Subhas Chandra Bose

3. Birth

  • Subhas Chandra Bose was born on 23 January 1897.
  • He was born at Cuttack in Odisha, then part of the Bengal Presidency.
📌 Must-Memorise

Subhas Bose → 23 January 1897 → Cuttack

4. Father

  • His father was Janakinath Bose.
  • Janakinath Bose was a prominent lawyer.
📌 Must-Memorise

Father → Janakinath Bose

5. Mother

  • His mother was Prabhavati Devi.
📌 Must-Memorise

Mother → Prabhavati Devi

6. Large Family

  • Subhas Bose was born into a large Bengali family.
  • His elder brother Sarat Chandra Bose later became an important nationalist politician.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Sarat Chandra Bose → Elder Brother of Subhas Bose

7. School Education

  • Bose studied at the Protestant European School in Cuttack.
  • He later studied at Ravenshaw Collegiate School.
📌 Must-Memorise

Bose → Ravenshaw Collegiate School

8. Presidency College

  • Bose entered Presidency College in Calcutta.
  • His student years were marked by growing nationalist consciousness.

9. Presidency College Incident

  • Bose was expelled from Presidency College after an incident involving Professor E.F. Oaten and nationalist students.
  • Bose's exact personal role in the assault remained disputed.
⚠️ TNPSC Caution

Presidency College → Oaten Incident → Bose Expelled

10. Scottish Church College

  • Bose later studied at Scottish Church College in Calcutta.
📌 Must-Memorise

Bose → Scottish Church College

11. Philosophy

  • Bose graduated with honours in Philosophy from the University of Calcutta.

12. Swami Vivekananda's Influence

  • Swami Vivekananda's writings deeply influenced Bose's early intellectual development.
  • Bose admired Vivekananda's emphasis on:
  • Strength.
  • Service.
  • National regeneration.
📌 Must-Memorise

Major Spiritual-Intellectual Influence → Swami Vivekananda

13. Ramakrishna Tradition

  • Bose was also influenced by the spiritual ideas associated with Ramakrishna Paramahamsa and Vivekananda.

14. England

  • Bose travelled to England for higher studies and preparation for the Indian Civil Service examination.

15. Indian Civil Service Examination

  • Bose performed exceptionally well in the Indian Civil Service examination.
  • He secured a high rank.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Bose → Successfully Qualified for ICS

16. Resignation from ICS

  • Bose resigned from the Indian Civil Service before beginning a permanent career under British rule.
  • He regarded service under the colonial government as incompatible with his nationalist convictions.
📌 Must-Memorise

Bose → Resigned from ICS → 1921

17. Return to India

  • Bose returned to India in 1921.
  • He entered the national movement soon afterward.

18. C.R. Das

  • Chittaranjan Das became Bose's most important early political mentor.
📌 Must-Memorise

Political Mentor of Bose → C.R. Das

19. Deshbandhu

  • C.R. Das was popularly known as Deshbandhu.

20. Bengal Nationalism

  • Under C.R. Das, Bose became actively involved in nationalist politics in Bengal.

21. National College

  • Bose became associated with the National College in Calcutta.
  • The institution represented the nationalist education movement.

22. Bengal Provincial Congress

  • Bose became increasingly active in the Bengal Provincial Congress organisation.

23. Journalism

  • He was involved in nationalist journalism and publications linked with C.R. Das's political movement.

24. Non-Cooperation Movement

  • Bose entered active politics during the period of Gandhi's Non-Cooperation Movement.
  • He supported the anti-colonial struggle but later became critical of repeated suspension or limitation of mass movements.

25. Prince of Wales Boycott

  • Bose participated in nationalist mobilisation against the visit of the Prince of Wales in the early 1920s.
  • He was arrested by colonial authorities.

26. Calcutta Municipal Politics

  • C.R. Das became Mayor of Calcutta after Swarajist electoral success.
  • Bose served in an important executive role in the Calcutta Corporation.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

C.R. Das + Bose → Calcutta Municipal Administration

27. Chief Executive Officer

  • Bose became Chief Executive Officer of the Calcutta Corporation.
  • He attempted to Indianise and reform municipal administration.

28. Political Imprisonment

  • Bose was repeatedly imprisoned by the British government throughout his political career.

29. Mandalay Prison

  • In 1924, Bose was arrested and later detained in Mandalay Jail in Burma.
📌 Must-Memorise

Bose → Mandalay Imprisonment

30. Health Problems

  • Harsh prison conditions damaged Bose's health.
  • He was eventually released in 1927.

31. Rise After Release

  • After his release, Bose rapidly emerged as one of the leading younger Congress nationalists.

32. Bengal Congress Leadership

  • He became a major leader of the Bengal Provincial Congress.

33. Jawaharlal Nehru and Bose

  • During the late 1920s, Bose and Jawaharlal Nehru represented a younger generation demanding a more radical anti-imperialist programme.
📌 Must-Memorise

Young Radical Congress Leaders → Jawaharlal Nehru + Subhas Bose

34. Complete Independence

  • Bose favoured complete independence rather than Dominion Status.

35. Nehru Report Debate

  • The Nehru Report of 1928 proposed Dominion Status.
  • Bose and Jawaharlal Nehru considered this insufficient.

36. Independence for India League

  • Bose and Jawaharlal Nehru were associated with the Independence for India League.
📌 Must-Memorise

Independence for India League → Nehru + Bose

37. Calcutta Congress 1928

  • At the 1928 Calcutta session, younger nationalists pushed Congress toward a more uncompromising demand for independence.

38. Lahore Congress 1929

  • Congress finally adopted Purna Swaraj at Lahore in December 1929.
  • Bose strongly supported complete independence.

39. Civil Disobedience Movement

  • Bose participated in the nationalist politics surrounding the Civil Disobedience Movement.
  • He was repeatedly arrested and imprisoned.

40. Mayor of Calcutta

  • Bose was elected Mayor of Calcutta in 1930.
📌 Must-Memorise

Subhas Bose → Mayor of Calcutta → 1930

41. Imprisonment and Exile

  • During the 1930s, British authorities repeatedly detained Bose.
  • Health concerns led to periods of treatment and travel in Europe.

42. Bose in Europe

While in Europe, Bose:

  • Met political leaders.
  • Studied European political systems.
  • Built contacts with Indians abroad.
  • Publicised India's demand for independence.

43. The Indian Struggle

  • Bose wrote The Indian Struggle.
📌 Must-Memorise

The Indian Struggle → Subhas Chandra Bose

44. Scope of The Indian Struggle

  • The work analysed the development of India's nationalist movement and Bose's political outlook.
  • British authorities restricted its circulation in India for a time.

45. Bose's Political Outlook

Bose favoured:

  • Complete independence.
  • Strong central planning.
  • Rapid industrialisation.
  • Social and economic transformation.
  • Anti-imperialism.

46. Bose and Socialism

  • Bose was strongly influenced by socialist ideas.
  • He wanted political freedom to be accompanied by social and economic reconstruction.

47. Economic Planning

  • Bose believed independent India would require systematic economic planning.

48. Strong State

  • Bose envisaged a strong modern state capable of carrying out:
  • Industrialisation.
  • Planning.
  • Social reform.
⚠️ TNPSC Caution

Bose's Planning Ideas → Important Part of His Political Thought

49. Congress Presidency — Haripura

  • Subhas Chandra Bose was elected President of the Indian National Congress for the Haripura session in 1938.
📌 Must-Memorise

Haripura Congress → 1938 → Subhas Bose

50. Haripura

  • Haripura is located in Gujarat.
  • Bose delivered an important presidential address outlining his vision for independent India.

51. Haripura Presidential Address

Bose discussed:

  • Political independence.
  • Economic reconstruction.
  • Industrial development.
  • Planning.
  • Social justice.

52. National Planning Committee

  • During Bose's Congress presidency, the National Planning Committee was established in 1938.
📌 Must-Memorise

National Planning Committee → 1938

53. Chairman of National Planning Committee

  • Jawaharlal Nehru was appointed Chairman of the National Planning Committee.
📌 Must-Memorise

National Planning Committee Chairman → Jawaharlal Nehru

54. Bose and Planning

  • Bose strongly supported the creation of the planning body even though Nehru chaired it.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

National Planning Committee Established During Bose Presidency

Chairman → Nehru

55. International Crisis

  • By 1938–39, war in Europe appeared increasingly likely.
  • Bose believed Britain's coming difficulties should be used to intensify India's struggle.

56. Difference with Gandhi

Bose and Gandhi differed mainly over:

  • Timing of confrontation.
  • Mass struggle strategy.
  • Use of international circumstances.
  • Political-economic orientation.

57. Mutual Respect

  • Despite major political differences, Bose continued to express respect for Gandhi.
  • Their disagreements were strategic and ideological rather than simple personal hostility.
⚠️ TNPSC Caution

Bose vs Gandhi → Major Differences, But Not Personal Enmity Alone

58. 1939 Congress Presidential Election

  • Bose sought a second consecutive term as Congress president in 1939.
  • Gandhi's preferred candidate was Pattabhi Sitaramayya.

59. Pattabhi Sitaramayya

  • Pattabhi Sitaramayya was a senior Congress leader from Andhra.

60. Bose's Victory

  • Bose defeated Pattabhi Sitaramayya in the presidential election.
📌 Must-Memorise

1939 INC Election → Bose Defeated Pattabhi Sitaramayya

61. Tripuri Session

  • Bose's second Congress presidency was associated with the Tripuri session of 1939.
📌 Must-Memorise

Tripuri → 1939 → Subhas Bose

62. Tripuri Crisis

  • A majority of the Congress Working Committee remained politically closer to Gandhi.
  • Bose therefore found it difficult to function effectively as president.

63. Resignation as Congress President

  • Bose resigned from the Congress presidency in April 1939.
📌 Must-Memorise

Bose Resigned INC Presidency → 1939

64. Rajendra Prasad

  • Dr. Rajendra Prasad succeeded Bose as Congress president after his resignation.

65. Forward Bloc

  • Bose founded the Forward Bloc in 1939.
📌 Must-Memorise

Forward Bloc → 1939 → Subhas Chandra Bose

66. Original Purpose

  • Forward Bloc initially sought to unite the more radical and left-wing elements within the Congress.

67. Programme of Forward Bloc

It supported:

  • Complete independence.
  • Anti-imperialist struggle.
  • Radical economic change.
  • Mass mobilisation.

68. Bose and Congress Relationship

  • Bose's relationship with the Congress leadership deteriorated further after the Forward Bloc was formed.

69. Second World War

  • Britain entered the Second World War in September 1939.
  • India was declared at war without consultation with elected Indian representatives.

70. Bose's Strategy During War

  • Bose believed Britain should be confronted while it was weakened by war.
📌 Must-Memorise

Bose's Wartime Principle → Britain's Difficulty = Opportunity for Indian Independence

71. Anti-War Mobilisation

  • Bose organised campaigns demanding immediate Indian independence during the war.

72. Arrest in 1940

  • British authorities detained Bose in 1940 under wartime regulations.

73. Hunger Strike

  • Bose began a hunger strike in prison.
  • The government feared the political consequences of his deteriorating health.

74. Release and House Arrest

  • He was released from prison but placed under strict house surveillance at his family residence in Calcutta.

75. Elgin Road

  • Bose's family residence at Elgin Road, Calcutta, became the site of his famous escape.
📌 Must-Memorise

Bose Escape → Elgin Road, Calcutta

76. Great Escape

  • In January 1941, Bose secretly escaped from British surveillance.
📌 Must-Memorise

Bose Escaped from India → January 1941

77. Disguise

  • Bose travelled in disguise to avoid detection.
  • He used a Muslim/Pathan identity during part of the journey.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Bose's Escape → Disguise + Secret Route

78. Sisir Kumar Bose

  • Bose's nephew Sisir Kumar Bose drove him for an important part of the escape journey.
📌 Must-Memorise

Sisir Kumar Bose → Helped Netaji Escape

79. Gomoh

  • Bose travelled to Gomoh railway station during his escape route.
  • The station later became associated with his escape.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Gomoh → Bose's 1941 Escape

80. Peshawar

  • Bose travelled through northwestern India toward Peshawar.

81. Afghanistan

  • He crossed into Afghanistan and reached Kabul.
📌 Must-Memorise

Escape Route → Calcutta → Peshawar → Kabul

82. Further Route

  • From Afghanistan, Bose eventually travelled through the Soviet sphere to Germany.

83. Germany

  • Bose reached Germany in 1941.
  • He sought support for India's independence from Britain's wartime enemies.

84. Strategic Principle

  • Bose followed the logic that an enemy of British imperialism could potentially be used to advance Indian independence.
⚠️ TNPSC Caution

Bose's Axis Contacts → Tactical Anti-British Strategy; Historically Controversial

85. Free India Centre

  • Bose established the Free India Centre in Berlin.
📌 Must-Memorise

Free India Centre → Berlin → Bose

86. Azad Hind Radio

  • Bose used Azad Hind Radio to broadcast messages to Indians.
📌 Must-Memorise

Azad Hind Radio → Bose

87. Radio Propaganda

His broadcasts called for:

  • Independence.
  • Anti-British mobilisation.
  • Unity among Indians.

88. Indian Legion

  • Bose helped organise an Indian military formation in Europe from Indian prisoners of war captured in North Africa.
  • It became known as the Indian Legion or Free India Legion.
📌 Must-Memorise

Indian Legion → Bose → Germany

89. Indian Legion's Composition

  • It was composed largely of Indian soldiers who had previously served in British Indian forces and had been captured by Axis forces.

90. Bose and Hitler

  • Bose met Adolf Hitler in Germany in 1942.
  • Bose sought stronger German support for India's liberation.
⚠️ TNPSC Caution

Bose Sought Assistance from Axis Powers → Does Not Mean His Political Aims Were Identical to Their Ideologies

91. Limits of German Strategy

  • Germany's geographical distance from India reduced the practical military usefulness of the European route.

92. Japanese Advance

  • Japan's rapid expansion into Southeast Asia created a more direct military theatre near India.
  • Bose therefore sought to shift his activities to East Asia.

93. Submarine Journey

  • Bose left Europe in 1943 aboard a German submarine.
  • He transferred at sea to a Japanese submarine.
📌 Must-Memorise

Bose Germany → East Asia → Submarine Journey, 1943

94. Unusual Wartime Journey

  • His submarine transfer from a German to a Japanese vessel in the Indian Ocean was an extraordinary wartime operation.

95. Arrival in East Asia

  • Bose reached East Asia in 1943.
  • He proceeded to Japan and then Southeast Asia.

96. Rash Behari Bose

  • Before Subhas Bose arrived, Rash Behari Bose had played a central role in organising Indian nationalists in East and Southeast Asia.
📌 Must-Memorise

Rash Behari Bose → Indian Independence League

97. Indian Independence League

  • The Indian Independence League organised Indian expatriates in Southeast Asia for the anti-British cause.

98. Rash Behari vs Subhas Bose

⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Rash Behari Bose ≠ Subhas Chandra Bose

They were different revolutionary leaders.

99. First INA

  • The first Indian National Army was organised in 1942.
📌 Must-Memorise

First INA → 1942

100. Captain Mohan Singh

  • Captain Mohan Singh was the principal military leader associated with the formation of the first INA.
📌 Must-Memorise

First INA → Captain Mohan Singh

101. Indian POWs

  • The INA drew heavily from Indian soldiers captured by Japanese forces in:
  • Malaya.
  • Singapore.
  • Southeast Asian campaigns.

102. Fall of Singapore

  • Singapore fell to Japan in February 1942.
  • Large numbers of Indian troops became prisoners of war.
📌 Must-Memorise

Singapore Fell to Japan → 1942

103. First INA Crisis

  • The first INA collapsed after disagreements between Mohan Singh and Japanese authorities.

104. Need for New Leadership

  • Indian nationalist organisers in Southeast Asia increasingly wanted Subhas Bose to assume leadership.

105. Bose Reaches Singapore

  • Subhas Bose arrived in Singapore in July 1943.
📌 Must-Memorise

Netaji → Singapore → July 1943

106. Leadership Transfer

  • Rash Behari Bose transferred leadership of the Indian Independence League to Subhas Chandra Bose.
📌 Must-Memorise

Rash Behari Bose → Leadership Transferred to Subhas Bose

107. Reorganisation of INA

  • Subhas Bose reorganised and revitalised the Indian National Army.
📌 Must-Memorise

Reorganised INA → Subhas Chandra Bose

108. Netaji and INA

  • Bose became the supreme political and military symbol of the INA movement.

109. Delhi Chalo

  • Bose gave the rallying call "Delhi Chalo" or "On to Delhi."
📌 Must-Memorise

Delhi Chalo → Subhas Chandra Bose / INA

110. Give Me Blood

Bose's famous call was:

  • "Give me blood, and I will give you freedom."
📌 Must-Memorise

"Give Me Blood..." → Netaji

111. Jai Hind

  • "Jai Hind" became one of the most famous slogans of the INA and Bose's movement.
  • Abid Hasan Safrani is widely credited with devising or popularising the greeting within Bose's circle.
⚠️ TNPSC Caution

Jai Hind → Closely Associated with Bose and INA

112. INA Motto

The INA/Azad Hind movement prominently used ideas expressed as:

  • Unity.
  • Faith.
  • Sacrifice.

Often rendered as:

  • Ittehad/Ittefaq.
  • Itmad.
  • Qurbani.

113. Religious Unity

  • Bose deliberately emphasised unity among:
  • Hindus.
  • Muslims.
  • Sikhs.
  • Christians.
  • The INA sought to minimise communal divisions.

114. Provisional Government of Free India

  • Bose proclaimed the Provisional Government of Free India on 21 October 1943.
📌 Must-Memorise

Azad Hind Government → 21 October 1943

115. Hindi Name

  • It was known as the Arzi Hukumat-e-Azad Hind.

116. Location

  • The government was proclaimed at Singapore.
📌 Must-Memorise

Azad Hind Government → Singapore

117. Bose's Positions

Bose served as:

  • Head of State.
  • Prime Minister.
  • Minister connected with war and foreign affairs.

118. International Recognition

  • The Azad Hind Government received recognition from Japan and several other Axis-aligned or Japanese-supported governments.
⚠️ TNPSC Caution

Recognition → Limited to Axis/Associated States, Not Universal

119. Declaration of War

  • The Azad Hind Government declared war against Britain and the United States.

120. Azad Hind Flag

  • The Azad Hind movement used a tricolour carrying a springing tiger emblem.
📌 Must-Memorise

INA/Azad Hind Flag → Springing Tiger

121. Azad Hind Institutions

The government attempted to develop symbols and institutions of sovereignty including:

  • Flag.
  • Currency-related instruments.
  • Stamps.
  • Diplomatic representation.
  • Military command.

122. Andaman and Nicobar Islands

  • Japan transferred nominal authority over the Andaman and Nicobar Islands to the Azad Hind Government in late 1943.
📌 Must-Memorise

Andaman–Nicobar → Azad Hind Government

123. Bose at Port Blair

  • Bose visited Port Blair in December 1943.
  • He ceremonially raised the Indian tricolour.

124. Renaming of Islands

Bose renamed:

  • Andaman → Shaheed.
  • Nicobar → Swaraj.
📌 Must-Memorise

Andaman → Shaheed

Nicobar → Swaraj

125. Actual Control — Caution

  • Japanese military authorities continued to exercise effective control over the islands despite the nominal transfer.
⚠️ TNPSC Caution

Azad Hind Sovereignty over Islands → Mostly Nominal

126. INA Structure

INA forces were organised into brigades and regiments named after important nationalist figures.

Names included:

  • Gandhi Brigade.
  • Nehru Brigade.
  • Azad Brigade.

127. Subhas Brigade

  • INA formations also included units directly associated with Bose's leadership.

128. Shah Nawaz Khan

  • Shah Nawaz Khan became an important INA commander.
📌 Must-Memorise

Shah Nawaz Khan → INA

129. Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon

  • Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon was another prominent INA officer.

130. Prem Kumar Sahgal

  • Prem Kumar Sahgal was also a major INA officer.

131. INA Trial Trio

Remember:

  • Shah Nawaz Khan.
  • Prem Kumar Sahgal.
  • Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon.
📌 Must-Memorise

Red Fort INA Trial → Shah Nawaz + Sahgal + Dhillon

132. Rani of Jhansi Regiment

  • Bose established an all-women military unit called the Rani of Jhansi Regiment.
📌 Must-Memorise

Rani of Jhansi Regiment → INA Women's Regiment

133. Lakshmi Swaminathan

  • Dr. Lakshmi Swaminathan became the commander of the Rani of Jhansi Regiment.
  • She later became widely known as Captain Lakshmi Sahgal.
📌 Must-Memorise

Captain Lakshmi → Rani of Jhansi Regiment

134. Tamil Nadu Link — Lakshmi Sahgal

  • Lakshmi Swaminathan was born in Madras.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Captain Lakshmi Sahgal → Born in Madras → INA

135. Mother of Lakshmi

  • Lakshmi's mother was Ammu Swaminathan, a prominent social and political activist.
🔗 Tamil Nadu Key Link

Ammu Swaminathan → Mother of Lakshmi Sahgal

136. Significance of Women's Regiment

  • The Rani of Jhansi Regiment symbolised Bose's belief in women's active participation in the struggle for independence.

137. Headquarters Shift

  • As military operations moved toward Burma and India, Bose and INA activities increasingly centred around Rangoon and the Burma front.

138. Japanese U-Go Offensive

  • In 1944, Japanese forces launched a major offensive toward India.
  • INA units participated alongside them.

139. Imphal Campaign

  • The campaign sought to enter India through Manipur and advance toward Imphal.
📌 Must-Memorise

INA + Japanese Campaign → Imphal → 1944

140. Kohima

  • Kohima in Nagaland became another major battlefield of the Japanese advance.
📌 Must-Memorise

Imphal + Kohima → 1944

141. INA Enters Indian Territory

  • INA forces entered parts of northeastern India during the 1944 campaign.

142. Moirang

  • Moirang in Manipur became one of the most important INA-associated locations in India.
📌 Must-Memorise

Moirang → INA → Manipur

143. Shaukat Malik

  • Colonel Shaukat Malik of the INA is associated with raising the Azad Hind flag at Moirang in April 1944.
📌 Must-Memorise

Moirang Flag → Shaukat Malik → 1944

144. Symbolic Importance of Moirang

  • Moirang became celebrated as a place where INA authority was symbolically established on Indian soil.

145. Imphal–Kohima Failure

The Axis offensive failed because of:

  • Strong Allied resistance.
  • Supply shortages.
  • Difficult terrain.
  • Monsoon.
  • Disease.
  • Allied air superiority.

146. INA Logistics

  • INA forces faced extreme shortages of:
  • Food.
  • Medicine.
  • Ammunition.
  • Transport.

147. Retreat

  • Japanese and INA forces were forced to retreat from the India-Burma frontier.

148. Heavy Losses

  • The retreat caused severe casualties due to:
  • Combat.
  • Disease.
  • Starvation.
  • Exhaustion.

149. Rangoon

  • Rangoon became a major political and military centre for the Azad Hind movement during the Burma campaign.

150. Azad Hind Bank

  • The Azad Hind movement established financial institutions to support its government and military activities.
  • Rangoon became an important centre of these activities.

151. Support from Indian Diaspora

  • Indian communities in Southeast Asia contributed:
  • Money.
  • Jewellery.
  • Supplies.
  • Volunteers.
📌 Must-Memorise

INA Support Base → Indians in Southeast Asia

152. Fundraising

  • Bose conducted major fundraising campaigns among expatriate Indian communities.

153. "Father of Our Nation"

  • In a 1944 broadcast, Bose appealed to Mahatma Gandhi and addressed him as "Father of our Nation."
📌 Must-Memorise

"Father of Our Nation" Address to Gandhi → Subhas Bose, 1944

154. Gandhi and Bose — Mutual Recognition

  • Bose regarded Gandhi as a central moral figure of the freedom struggle despite their political differences.
  • Gandhi, in turn, recognised Bose's patriotism and sacrifice.

155. Gandhi Brigade

  • Naming an INA brigade after Gandhi illustrates Bose's continued symbolic respect for him.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Bose-Gandhi Difference ≠ Rejection of Gandhi's National Importance

156. 1944–45 Turning Point

  • Allied victories gradually reversed Japanese expansion in Burma.
  • INA's military position deteriorated rapidly.

157. Fall of Rangoon

  • Allied forces recaptured Rangoon in 1945.
  • INA forces fragmented or surrendered during the wider Japanese retreat.

158. End of INA Military Campaign

  • Japan's impending defeat made continued INA military operations impossible.

159. Bose Leaves Southeast Asian Front

  • Bose attempted to move eastward as Japanese power collapsed.

160. Reported Plane Crash

  • According to the generally accepted wartime account, Bose was seriously injured in an aircraft crash at Taihoku in Japanese-occupied Taiwan on 18 August 1945.
📌 Must-Memorise

Reported Death of Bose → 18 August 1945 → Taihoku

161. Taihoku

  • Taihoku is present-day Taipei in Taiwan.
📌 Must-Memorise

Taihoku → Present-Day Taipei

162. Reported Cause of Death

  • Contemporary accounts stated that Bose died from severe burn injuries in a military hospital after the crash.

163. Death Controversy

  • Bose's death became the subject of continuing public controversy.
  • Different investigations examined whether he died in the 1945 crash.
⚠️ TNPSC Caution

For Exams → Standard Historical Date Usually 18 August 1945

Death Circumstances → Long-Standing Controversy

164. Shah Nawaz Committee

  • The Government of India appointed the Shah Nawaz Committee in the 1950s to investigate Bose's disappearance.
  • It concluded that Bose died in the plane crash.

165. Khosla Commission

  • A later commission headed by Justice G.D. Khosla also concluded that Bose died in the 1945 crash.

166. Mukherjee Commission

  • The Justice Mukherjee Commission later questioned the plane-crash conclusion.
  • The Government of India did not accept its conclusion on this point.
⚠️ TNPSC Caution

Bose Death → Investigation Findings Have Differed

167. Renkoji Temple

  • Ashes believed to be those of Bose have been kept at Renkoji Temple in Tokyo.
⚠️ TNPSC Caution

Renkoji Ashes → Believed/Claimed to Be Bose's

168. INA After Bose

  • Thousands of INA soldiers became prisoners of the British after the war.

169. Decision to Hold Trials

  • British authorities decided to prosecute selected INA officers for offences including waging war against the King-Emperor.

170. Red Fort Trials

  • The first famous INA trial was held at the Red Fort in Delhi in 1945.
📌 Must-Memorise

INA Trials → Red Fort → 1945–46

171. First Trial

The three famous defendants were:

  • Shah Nawaz Khan.
  • Prem Kumar Sahgal.
  • Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon.

172. Religious Symbolism of Trio

The three officers were:

  • Muslim.
  • Hindu.
  • Sikh.

Their joint trial became a powerful symbol of national unity.

🔗 TNPSC Key Link

INA Trial Trio → Communal Unity Symbol

173. Defence Committee

Prominent lawyers involved in defence efforts included:

  • Bhulabhai Desai.
  • Tej Bahadur Sapru.
  • K.N. Katju.
  • Asaf Ali.
  • Jawaharlal Nehru.

174. Jawaharlal Nehru at INA Trial

  • Nehru appeared in legal robes in support of the INA defence.
📌 Must-Memorise

Nehru → INA Defence at Red Fort

175. Public Response

INA trials generated:

  • Demonstrations.
  • Student protests.
  • Fundraising.
  • Cross-community sympathy.

176. Congress and INA

  • Congress had disagreed with Bose's wartime strategy.
  • Nevertheless, Congress strongly defended INA prisoners after the war.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Congress Political Difference with Bose → But Supported INA Defendants

177. Sentences

  • The first defendants were convicted.
  • Their sentences were ultimately remitted under intense political and public pressure.

178. Impact of INA Trials

The trials:

  • Increased anti-British sentiment.
  • Enhanced Bose's posthumous prestige.
  • Undermined unquestioning loyalty within sections of the colonial armed forces.

179. Royal Indian Navy Revolt

  • The Royal Indian Navy uprising occurred in February 1946.

RIN Revolt → 1946

  • INA trials formed part of the wider political atmosphere that affected Indian servicemen after World War II.
  • The precise extent to which INA alone caused later military unrest is debated.

INA Trials → Major Psychological Impact

Do Not Treat as Sole Cause of RIN Revolt

181. Bose's Concept of National Unity

He strongly promoted unity across:

  • Religion.
  • Region.
  • Caste.
  • Language.

182. Bose and Secular Nationalism

  • Bose's political nationalism was secular in orientation.
  • The INA deliberately used multi-religious symbols and leadership.

183. Bose and Women

  • Bose advocated active political and military participation of women.
  • The Rani of Jhansi Regiment embodied this view.

184. Bose and Youth

  • Bose had especially strong appeal among:
  • Students.
  • Young nationalists.
  • Radical Congress workers.

185. Bose and Labour

  • Bose supported labour organisation and broader social-economic transformation.
  • His nationalist vision included workers and peasants.

186. Bose and Industrialisation

  • He favoured rapid heavy industrial development in independent India.

187. Bose and Planning

His economic ideas included:

  • State planning.
  • Industrialisation.
  • Modern science.
  • Reduction of poverty.

188. Bose and Social Equality

  • Bose opposed caste and communal divisions.
  • He saw national unity as necessary for freedom.

189. Bose's View of Freedom

For Bose, independence meant:

  • End of British rule.
  • Political sovereignty.
  • Economic reconstruction.
  • Social transformation.

190. Bose vs Moderate Politics

Bose rejected reliance primarily on:

  • Petitions.
  • Slow constitutional concessions.

He favoured:

  • Direct confrontation.
  • Mass mobilisation.
  • International pressure.

191. Bose vs Gandhian Strategy

Gandhi:

  • Ahimsa.
  • Satyagraha.
  • Mass civil resistance.

Bose:

  • Mass mobilisation.
  • Stronger confrontation.
  • Willingness to use armed struggle in wartime circumstances.
🔗 TNPSC Favourite Comparison

Both → Independence

Methods → Different

192. Bose vs Revolutionary Secret Societies

  • Bose did not begin his career merely as a secret revolutionary.
  • He spent much of his political life within the Congress and mass politics before turning to international armed struggle.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Bose → Congress Mass Leader Before INA Leader

193. Bose and Fascism — Caution

  • Bose sought assistance from Germany, Italy and Japan because they were fighting Britain.
  • His wartime alliances remain historically controversial.
  • His own stated political objective was Indian independence.
⚠️ TNPSC Caution

Axis Alliance → Tactical Wartime Strategy; Do Not Simplify into Identity of Ideology

194. Azad Hind Government Significance

It attempted to demonstrate that:

  • Indians could establish an independent government.
  • The struggle had entered an international and military phase.

195. INA Military Significance

  • The INA did not defeat British forces militarily.
  • Its greatest historical impact came partly through:
  • Symbolism.
  • Post-war trials.
  • Nationalist mobilisation.
📌 Must-Memorise

INA → Limited Battlefield Success, Major Political-Psychological Impact

196. INA and Indian Army

  • British concern increased over the loyalty and political mood of Indian armed forces after the war.

197. Bose's Legacy

Bose is remembered for:

  • Complete independence.
  • Anti-imperialist militancy.
  • Military nationalism.
  • Secular unity.
  • Economic planning.
  • Personal sacrifice.

198. Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Jayanti

  • 23 January marks Bose's birth anniversary.

199. Parakram Diwas

  • In modern official commemoration, 23 January is observed as Parakram Diwas.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

23 January → Netaji's Birth Anniversary

200. Tamil Nadu Link — INA Recruitment

  • Large numbers of Indians living in Malaya, Singapore and Burma had ancestral roots in Tamil-speaking areas.
  • Tamil expatriates therefore formed an important social base for the INA and Azad Hind movement.

Southeast Asian Tamil Diaspora → Important INA Support Base

203. Janaki Athi Nahappan

  • Janaki Athi Nahappan, a young woman of Tamil origin in Malaya, became associated with the Rani of Jhansi Regiment and later public life in Malaysia.

  • Established Azad Hind Government.
  • Mobilised Indian diaspora.
  • Encouraged women's military participation.
  • Strengthened post-war anti-colonial sentiment.

  • National service.
